<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="טבת_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916328_theRebbe_715" batchId="meluket-_D7_98_D7_91_D7_AA_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916328_theRebbe_715__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>There are multiple opinions on the age at which Avraham recognized his Creator, showing different levels of recognition, and the revelation of "I am Kel Shakkai" introduced a new aspect of G‑dliness he had not known before.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And further proof of this:</t>
    <t s="1">It is stated in the Gemara,</t>
    <t s="2">"At three years old, Avraham recognized his Creator."</t>
    <t s="3">And in the Rambam,</t>
    <t s="4">it is stated that at forty years old he recognized his Creator.</t>
    <t s="5">And there is another opinion</t>
    <t s="6">(in the Midrash)</t>
    <t s="7">that at forty-eight years old he recognized his Creator.</t>
    <t s="8">And it is explained elsewhere</t>
    <t s="9">that this is not a dispute about the factual reality,</t>
    <t s="10">for there are many and varied levels in this.</t>
    <t s="11">Accordingly,</t>
    <t s="12">if we say that in the Holy One, blessed be He's statement to Avraham, "I am Kel Shakkai," only the G‑dliness within creation was revealed to him</t>
    <t s="13">(that I said to My world, "Enough"),</t>
    <t s="14">we must say</t>
    <t s="15">that what the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Avraham</t>
    <t s="16">(when he was ninety-nine years old)</t>
    <t s="17">"I am Kel Shakkai,"</t>
    <t s="18">even though many years before this he had recognized his Creator,</t>
    <t s="19">is</t>
    <t s="20">that previously he recognized his Creator through intellectual compulsion and the like,</t>
    <t s="21">and this is not comparable to the knowledge and recognition that comes through revelation from Above.</t>
    <t s="22">But from the fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him "I am Kel Shakkai"</t>
    <t s="23">(in the language of a novel concept)</t>
    <t s="24">it implies that with this statement, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed to him a new matter that he had not known before.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The name Shakkai has two interpretations: "I said to My world, 'Enough'" (limitation) and "My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature" (abundant sufficiency), and the novelty revealed to the Patriarchs was the latter meaning.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="2">as explained in the discourses,</t>
    <t s="3">that the name Shakkai has two interpretations.</t>
    <t s="4">"I said to My world, 'Enough,'"</t>
    <t s="5">and "My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature."</t>
    <t s="6">And the difference between the two interpretations</t>
    <t s="7">(the concepts)</t>
    <t s="8">is,</t>
    <t s="9">both in the interpretation of the word "Dai" (enough/sufficient) and in the subject that the word "Dai" speaks about.</t>
    <t s="10">According to the interpretation that the name Shakkai is "I said to My world, 'Enough,'"</t>
    <t s="11">the word "Dai" speaks about the world</t>
    <t s="12">(that I said to My world, "Enough"),</t>
    <t s="13">and the meaning of "Dai" is limitation,</t>
    <t s="14">that the world should be in limitation and should not stretch forth and continue.</t>
    <t s="15">And according to the interpretation that the name Shakkai is "My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature,"</t>
    <t s="16">the word "Dai" speaks about G‑dliness</t>
    <t s="17">(that My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature),</t>
    <t s="18">and the meaning of "Dai" is a very great abundance that is enough and sufficient for every creature.</t>
    <t s="19">Analogous to "sufficient for his lack, which is lacking to him,"</t>
    <t s="20">a great abundance that fills all his lack,</t>
    <t s="21">even a horse to ride upon and a servant to run before him.</t>
    <t s="22">[And although "sufficient for his lack" is also within limitation,</t>
    <t s="23">"sufficient for his lack" and you are not commanded to enrich him,</t>
    <t s="24">the emphasis in "sufficient for his lack" is not on the limitation but on the abundance that fills all his lack.]</t>
    <t s="25">And this is the novelty in "I appeared to the Patriarchs"</t>
    <t s="26">as Kel Shakkai,</t>
    <t s="27">beginning with Avraham, to whom it was said "I am Kel Shakkai,"</t>
    <t s="28">relative to the name Shakkai that was in creation,</t>
    <t s="29">for the name Shakkai that was at the creation of the world is on account of "I said to My world, 'Enough,'"</t>
    <t s="30">and the name Shakkai that was revealed to Avraham</t>
    <t s="31">[and likewise to Yitzchak and Yaakov]</t>
    <t s="32">is on account of "My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The revelation of Kel Shakkai to the Patriarchs, meaning "My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature," is lower than the revelation of the name Havayah and includes miracles that are clothed in nature.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, even the revelation of Kel Shakkai that was revealed to the Patriarchs,</t>
    <t s="2">on account of "My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature,"</t>
    <t s="3">is lower than the revelation of the name Havayah,</t>
    <t s="4">"And I appeared to the Patriarchs as Kel Shakkai, but My name Havayah I did not make known to them."</t>
    <t s="5">And it is explained in the discourses,</t>
    <t s="6">that in the revelation of the name Shakkai on account of "My G‑dliness is sufficient for every creature," the matter of miracles is also included.</t>
    <t s="7">For since the matter of "sufficient in My G‑dliness for every creature" is analogous to "sufficient for his lack," whose meaning is whatever is lacking to him,</t>
    <t s="8">it is therefore understood,</t>
    <t s="9">that even when the creatures</t>
    <t s="10">(every creature)</t>
    <t s="11">will need a miracle,</t>
    <t s="12">the G‑dliness of the name Shakkai is sufficient to fill for them even this lack.</t>
    <t s="13">However, the miracles that are drawn from the name Shakkai are miracles that are clothed in nature,</t>
    <t s="14">and miracles that are above nature,</t>
    <t s="15">their drawing down is from the name Havayah.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
